finding.claim: collect uses forEach with async callback without awaiting, so it returns empty results before tasks complete and try/catch cannot observe rejections
finding.title: async forEach not awaited returns empty results

verifier.reason: The code at src/analytics.ts:6-12 uses tasks.forEach with an async callback and immediately returns results without awaiting those callbacks, so the array is returned before awaited tasks complete and rejections bypass the try/catch at src/analytics.ts:9.

finding.claim: buildSummary posts to module-global totals then summarizes totals instead of the passed entries, so repeated calls accumulate prior entries
finding.title: summary aggregates global totals instead of argument

verifier.reason: Confirmed at src/ledger.ts:6 the totals array is module-global, src/ledger.ts:13 buildSummary appends via post(entries) without clearing it, and src/ledger.ts:15 it aggregates totals rather than the passed entries, so repeated calls accumulate.

finding.claim: validate uses OR instead of AND for undefined/null checks, so conditions are always true and errors are always reported
finding.title: OR instead of AND makes validation always fail

verifier.reason: At src/validation.ts:8 and src/validation.ts:11, `!== undefined || !== null` is always true because a value cannot be both undefined and null, so errors are always pushed at src/validation.ts:9 and src/validation.ts:12.

finding.claim: rotateToken does not await store.save before store.get, so read can race the write and return stale token
finding.title: missing await on save before get

verifier.reason: At src/session.ts:11 store.save(userId, token) is called without await despite SessionStore.save returning Promise<void> at src/session.ts:2, and src/session.ts:12 immediately returns store.get(userId), so the read can race the write and return a stale token.

finding.claim: pageSlice uses slice(start, end+1) where end is already start+size, returning size+1 elements instead of size
finding.title: off-by-one slice returns extra element

verifier.reason: Confirmed: at src/paging.ts:9 end is already start+size and Array.slice's end is exclusive, so src/paging.ts:10 slice(start, end+1) returns up to size+1 elements instead of size.

finding.claim: sortScores calls sort without numeric comparator, so numbers sort lexicographically (e.g. 10 before 9)
finding.title: numeric sort without comparator

verifier.reason: The code at src/scores.ts:2 calls scores.slice().sort() with no comparator, so JavaScript's default string conversion sorts numbers lexicographically (e.g. 10 before 9).

finding.claim: withinQuota uses strict < but documented max is inclusive, so exact-max requests are incorrectly rejected; should be <=
finding.title: exclusive quota check contradicts inclusive max

verifier.reason: The documentation at src/quota.ts:2-3 states max is inclusive and exact-max use is within quota, but src/quota.ts:6 returns used + amount < max, so an exact-max request returns false.

finding.claim: normalizeSettings uses || fallback so legitimate 0 values become 20/1000; should use ??

evidence.snippet: // Optional values are read from settings where 0 is a legitimate value.

finding.title: OR fallback discards legitimate zero

verifier.reason: The code at src/settings.ts:13-14 uses `raw.pageSize || 20` and `raw.budgetCents || 1000`, so 0 is falsy and is replaced, while src/settings.ts:18 states 0 is a legitimate value for settings.
